Eur Urol 62(5):834-40, Nov 2012; quote verbatim. Full text paywalled; Intro cites dog micturition-threshold model and Discussion opens with animal-model premise before result, so comparison_stated could be true. Ritobegron: no primary source, same stands.
Quote verbatim. Model nit: the filed safety-pharmacology model (EPAR) was conscious dog/monkey telemetry plus hERG, broader than cloned beta1/beta2 selectivity; acceptable for the 2007 pivotal paper.

Ohlstein makes no model-vs-patient safety comparison (abstract/intro/discussion seen); juxtaposed by drafter, so untested on this source. Re-source to EMA Betmiga CHMP report 18 Oct 2012, which states dog/monkey HR and QT predictions against human results.

missing: Safety: EMA CHMP assessment report EMA/706651/2012 (18 Oct 2012), https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/assessment-report/betmiga-epar-public-assessment-report_en.pdf, states the comparison: dog HR up at >=0.03 mg/kg 'at doses lower than those proposed clinically', monkey HR up at 10 mg/kg (Cmax 29.6x MRHD); 'In humans at the MRHD the heart rate increase was limited to approximately 1 bpm.' And: 'Non clinical studies in dogs and monkeys did not indicate any potential for QT prolongation in man at the proposed clinical dose of 50 mg', set beside the TQT (Malik 2012, PMID 23149929: no QTcI prolongation at 50/100 mg, prolongation at 200 mg in females only, confirmed). Fields: comparison_stated true, model_filed true, subjects mixed, magnitude direction_only, source_calls_it null.

Safety caveat: the same EPAR reports dog systolic/mean BP 'significantly decreased at 0.3 to 10 mg/kg', whereas the Myrbetriq label 5.1 (DailyMed setid ba9e9e15-e666-4c56-9271-2e24739cfa2d) says BP increased ~3.5/1.5 mmHg vs placebo at 50 mg in healthy volunteers and ~0.5-1 mmHg in OAB patients. A directional BP miss the reviewer never draws; see rule_questions.

Registry dates confirmed via ClinicalTrials.gov API: SCORPIO NCT00689104, ARIES NCT00662909 and CAPRICORN NCT00912964 all results-first-posted 2012-10-17 (submitted 2012-07-11/17). Draft names only ARIES. NCT00343486 (Ohlstein) and NCT01004315 (ritobegron) have no results and no completion date; registry_date null is correct.

Ritobegron Phase 3 miss: PubMed has no clinical efficacy report (13 hits: rat/monkey pharmacology, a DDI study in healthy men, reviews); EU-CTR returns no record for ritobegron; CT.gov NCT01004315 has no results. The only report is trade press (Scrip SC075576, 'Kissei Over Active Bladder Agent Phase III Fails To Meet Endpoint', sponsor preliminary analysis, undated in the result). Not a primary source under rule 1.
FDA 202611Orig1s000 PharmR/ClinPharmR: accessdata returned its abuse-detection page to curl; not circumvented. The EMA EPAR carries the same nonclinical telemetry material and was used instead.
rule_questions: Rule 1 names FDA label/review; does an EMA CHMP assessment report qualify as a primary regulatory review? If yes, safety 2012 same is sustainable with comparison_stated=true (EPAR); if no, safety 2012 falls to untested because Ohlstein alone never compares model and patient safety.

Dog telemetry predicted a BP decrease; humans show a small BP increase carried as a label warning. The EPAR reports both in separate sections without contrasting them. Does a within-document juxtaposition count as a 'published comparison' for contra? If so safety becomes contra (2012) despite HR direction and therapeutic-dose QT matching.

Ritobegron failed its Phase 3 primary endpoint after positive rat and monkey cystometry, which is the contra pattern, but the only evidence is a sponsor announcement via trade press (no DOI, no registry results, no EU-CTR record). Rule 1 excludes it, so efficacy stays same; should sponsor announcements be admitted with a low-confidence tag? Announcement date unknown (NCT last updated 2010-07); if before Nov 2012 it would precede the same entry.

Ohlstein frames the trial as the test of the animal-model premise (Intro cites the dog model; Discussion opens 'effective in every animal model of detrusor overactivity ever tested ... Against this background, we have performed a clinical proof-of-concept study') but gives no quantitative side-by-side. Is that comparison_stated true or false? Draft chose false.

The dog model over-predicted HR liability (effects below the clinical dose vs ~1 bpm in humans at MRHD). The status table has no 'liability over-predicted' category: same with magnitude direction_only, or a scaling miss?
